documents.title: SIT Institutional Memory Platform — Detailed Design

constraints.text: PDPA compliance: audit trails are required for every operation on personal data.
Vector-store infrastructure cost must stay within SGD 800-1,200/month at 15,000-learner scale (Azure Singapore region, Memory Optimised 16-vCore tier).
SIT-AI-Factory-RAG (Azure AI Search) is a separate system, in a separate resource group, with no shared infrastructure.
The ten foundational principles override any later section that appears to conflict with them.
HIGHLY_RESTRICTED data must sit in a physically separate schema (memory_sensitive) with separate database credentials.
Platform stack: Azure Database for PostgreSQL + pgvector, Entra ID / OAuth 2.0, Kafka (Azure Event Hubs), Redis, and Azure OpenAI text-embedding-3-small.

doc_anchors.quote: This document describes the architecture of the SIT Institutional Memory Platform - a governed memory
Memory infrastructure for AI Tutor, AI Buddy, Academic Advisory, Counselling, Career, and Orientation agents
SIT-AI-Factory-RAG (the Azure AI Search RAG project) - a separate system, in a separate resource group, with

key_assumptions.text: About 600 vectors per learner across a full degree, giving about 9.5M vectors at 15,000 learners (including alumni and institution-level vectors).
Queries are always filtered by learner_id + slot_path, so the effective search space per query is 500-800 vectors, which supports 5-15 ms latency.
HNSW index overhead is about 1.4×, and the growth ceiling before degradation is about 30-40M vectors.
The MMP is not in the critical request path, so MMP downtime does not affect agent reads and writes.
The deferred items (cohort namespace, compaction, non-SIT identity) are not needed for the launch scope of the initial six agents.
No open-source Memory Management Plane for agent memory exists (prior-art claim).
Azure Event Hubs is assumed to be the managed Kafka-API alternative (pending confirmation).

objectives.text: The learner namespace is authoritative and the agent's copy is backup only. Conflicts resolve in favour of the learner namespace.
Memory is private by default, shared by exception, and anonymised for service learning.
Access control is pre-retrieval: the namespace restriction gates the query itself, not the results after retrieval.
Counselling hard wall: wellbeing/counselling/ is HIGHLY_RESTRICTED, with zero cross-domain reads, no MMP override and no exceptions.
Agents share across each other only through the learner namespace and never access each other's memory directly.
No uncontrolled self-writing: all writes are classified and policy-checked before storage.
Every operation is audited (access, write, denial, compaction, deletion, escalation), as required for PDPA.
Write async via Kafka (non-blocking) and read cached via Redis L1 then PostgreSQL.
Administrators, not agents, configure slot templates, sensitivity levels and retention rules.
Minimum useful context: summary over transcript, fact over full conversation, and a token-budgeted context pack.
Provide an institution-level memory platform covering all six layers (capture, classification, storage, retrieval, governance, administration), not only layers 2-4 as in Mem0, Zep or Letta.
Be specified well enough for an engineering team or AI coding assistant to begin implementation (Section 28 self-assessment).

intent_summary.statement: The document describes the SIT Institutional Memory Platform. It is an institution-level, governed memory infrastructure, not a per-agent store. It serves six AI agents (Tutor, Buddy, Academic Advisory, Counselling, Career, Orientation) for about 15,000 SIT learners. Its main features are per-learner structured namespaces, pre-retrieval policy-enforced access control, a strict counselling isolation wall, PDPA-oriented audit of every operation, an async write path and cached read path, and an out-of-band Memory Management Plane for configuration and governance. The document is written to be detailed enough for an engineering team or AI coding assistant to start building, and Section 28 assesses where that is not yet true. The separate SIT-AI-Factory-RAG system is explicitly out of scope.

questions.question: Are the objectives, principles P1-P10, FR/NFR requirements and Section 25 confirmed decisions stated clearly and consistently enough to review against, and does the 'principle wins' rule settle conflicts such as Super Admin 'Everything' versus P4's no-override counselling wall?
questions.rationale: Every later finding is judged against these stated intents, so ambiguity in them (for example the precedence of Super Admin access over P4) affects every verdict.

queries: pgvector HNSW filtering WHERE clause fewer results iterative index scan
pgvector partial index partitioning filtered vector search
questions.question: When a pgvector HNSW index is combined with WHERE filters on learner_id and slot_path, does it return the full top-k from the 500-800 in-scope vectors, or can post-filtering of the approximate index return too few or no results? Does the design need iterative index scans, partitioning or a B-tree-first plan?
questions.rationale: NFR-2 and the Section 12 claim that the effective search space is 500-800 vectors depend on how pgvector actually filters HNSW results.

questions.question: Are the following error and rollback paths defined: async write failure after the immediate ACK (dead-letter handling, notifying the agent, idempotency); a Validator rejection that happens after the ACK; namespace and backup reconciliation after degraded mode; SIS webhook failures; and rollback of template publication? Section 26 acknowledges some of these, so what priority should each get?
questions.rationale: FR-9, FR-12 and FR-16 depend on these paths, and a write that is acknowledged and then rejected loses data silently, contrary to 'no silent errors'.

questions.question: Do sections contradict each other on: (a) MMP not being in the critical path (NFR-4) versus Gateway Check 4 calling the MMP to provision slots; (b) FR-9's order classify→embed→validate→route→audit versus validating before storage and embedding unknown keys; (c) policy decisions never cached (Section 16) versus Redis-cached context packs; (d) FR-1's nine areas at registration versus SIS provisioning only core/ and orientation/; (e) the PUBLIC tier and WORKING-type orientation keys versus the tier and store definitions?
questions.rationale: Contradictions between requirements and flows will either produce incorrect code or cause the acceptance tests in Section 27 to fail.

queries: Microsoft Entra ID access token lifetime default maximum configurable
Entra ID configurable token lifetime policy access token 1 day limit
Entra ID refresh token lifetime 90 days
questions.question: Can Entra ID OAuth 2.0 access tokens be valid for 48 hours (default and maximum configurable lifetimes), and does the design confuse access-token lifetime with refresh-token or session lifetime?
questions.rationale: NFR-6 and a confirmed decision fix a 48-hour token window that may be outside what Entra ID allows.

queries: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server memory optimized 16 vCore price Southeast Asia
Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server pgvector supported version
questions.question: Is SGD 800-1,200/month realistic for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server Memory Optimised 16 vCores / 128 GB in Southeast Asia, including storage, HA and backups, and does the pgvector extension supported there include the needed HNSW and iterative-scan features?
questions.rationale: NFR-10 and the confirmed SKU decision depend on this cost figure and on feature support.

queries: Singapore PDPA retention limitation obligation section 25
PDPC advisory guidelines retention limitation cease to retain
PDPA access and correction obligation withdrawal of consent
questions.question: Do Singapore PDPA obligations (retention limitation, access and correction, protection, breach notification) conflict with agent per-learner backups that survive learner self-deletion, with audit logs that are append-only and never modified, and with an unspecified audit retention period?
questions.rationale: P7 and FR-15 claim PDPA compliance, while Sections 13 and 20 keep data after a learner deletes it.

questions.question: Is the counselling hard wall complete across every storage path: the counsellor agent's own per-learner backup, Redis context-pack caching, the memory.write.sensitive topic, the cross-learner pattern derivation, the Super Admin role, and the Admin API, whose own authentication and authorisation are not specified?
questions.rationale: FR-5, P4 and NFR-5 promise zero exceptions, but HIGHLY_RESTRICTED data may persist or be exposed outside the memory_sensitive schema.

queries: pgvector HNSW index memory size 1536 dimensions millions vectors build time
Azure OpenAI text-embedding-3-small rate limits tokens per minute
questions.question: Does the design hold for 15,000 learners and ~9.5M vectors in a single 128 GB instance with high availability, and what happens when PostgreSQL, Redis or the embedding service fails (the BM25 fallback has no defined index; Azure OpenAI rate limits during re-embedding)?
questions.rationale: NFR-1 and NFR-2 and the degraded-mode behaviour depend on how these components fail and on the memory headroom for an ~80 GB index.

queries: Azure Event Hubs Kafka protocol support limitations
Azure Event Hubs quotas consumer groups throughput units standard premium
questions.question: Does Azure Event Hubs' Kafka endpoint support what the write path assumes (consumer groups, retries, ordering per partition, retention), and are there tier limits on throughput, retention or consumer groups that matter for term-start write spikes?
questions.rationale: The confirmed Kafka (Azure Event Hubs) write-path decision and the pending backlog item rely on Event Hubs behaving like Kafka.

questions.question: Which confirmed decisions or 'Ready' readiness ratings rest on pending items? Examples: the Dispatcher conflict resolution is in the backlog yet the Router is rated codeable; the Auditor is rated mostly ready although retention and PDPA sign-off are pending; Event Hubs is listed as a confirmed decision and also as pending; the Policy Engine algorithm is unspecified.
questions.rationale: Decisions marked confirmed while they depend on open items risk rework in build phases 3, 4 and 6.

questions.question: Can each Section 27 acceptance criterion verify its requirement? Specifically: FR-8 expects a DENY for every dimension, including Retention and Redaction; FR-13 expects exactly one audit entry per operation even though the async path produces several; the NFR-2 test drops the 5 ms lower bound; NFR-3 and FR-9 use an unspecified tolerance; NFR-6 is tested in a way that may not be realisable with Entra; and FR-6 relies on a static import check.
questions.rationale: Section 27 is the basis of the Build Phase 9 test plan, so a criterion that cannot fail or cannot be met leaves requirements unverified.

questions.question: Can the likely refinements (filtered-HNSW strategy, the token lifetime model, purging agent backups, policy precedence) be made while preserving the confirmed decisions on pgvector, the SKU, the 48-hour window, automatic write-back and the counselling wall, and is there at least two-source evidence for challenging any of them, such as the 48-hour token window?
questions.rationale: Rule 5 requires that approved decisions are preserved unless strong evidence shows one cannot meet an objective.

questions.question: Are owners named for template approval, DPO sign-off on retention and audit, Super Admin emergency access, cost monitoring, and operating the re-embedding backlog, and are monitoring and alerting for Kafka consumer lag, cache hit rate and degraded mode defined?
questions.rationale: The MMP roles in Section 21 are listed without accountable owners or decision gates, while the pending items in Section 26 need closure owners.
